They Called It the Barn

STS-HS11-L4-6501000-HSUSH-MKT-LAT-02 • HS US History & Geography • The Americanization Movement
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In 1931, the school board in Lemon Grove, California, built a small separate building for its Mexican American students and said it would help “Americanize” them. The families called it the barn, and they kept their children home instead of sending them there. A twelve-year-old student named Roberto Álvarez became the name on their lawsuit, and a judge in San Diego ruled that the students belonged back in the main school. Today, Marisol, Rafael, and Tomás are putting that case on trial again.
Americanization programs said they wanted to help families belong. Why do you think the Lemon Grove families felt the separate building did the opposite?
